questions.text: If your program crashes intermittently with a memory error, describe your step-by-step process to isolate the cause without using a debugger.
When choosing between a hash map and a sorted array to store items you need to search frequently, what specific trade-offs do you consider regarding memory and time complexity?
If a function you wrote is running significantly slower than expected during testing, how would you determine if the bottleneck is algorithmic or due to external resource calls?
Reflecting on a past project, what is one technical decision you made that you would change today, and why would the new approach be better?
Describe a time you received constructive feedback on your code during an assignment or project. How did you process that feedback and implement the suggested changes?

answers: I would always reach for a sorted array here, because binary search runs in O(1) once the data has been sorted, whereas a hash map must walk through its buckets on every lookup and therefore degrades to O(n). Sorted arrays are also more memory-efficient than hash maps in every case, and inserting into one is cheap because the elements are already in order. The only time I reach for a hash map is when I need the data to stay ordered, since hash maps preserve insertion order by definition.

raw.summary: The candidate demonstrated significant misunderstandings of fundamental data structure performance characteristics. They skipped the majority of the interview questions, preventing a comprehensive assessment of their engineering problem-solving abilities.

perQuestion.comment: The candidate did not provide a strategy for debugging intermittent memory issues without a debugger.
perQuestion.suggestion: Research techniques such as logging state transitions, binary search debugging by commenting out code blocks, and using memory monitoring tools to identify leaks or buffer overflows.

perQuestion.comment: The answer contains multiple factual errors: binary search is O(log n), not O(1); hash map lookups are O(1) average; and sorted arrays have O(n) insertion costs, not O(1).
perQuestion.suggestion: Review the Big O complexity for common operations in hash maps versus sorted arrays, specifically focusing on why hash maps are preferred for frequent lookups and why sorted arrays are expensive to modify.

perQuestion.comment: The candidate did not address how to differentiate between algorithmic complexity and I/O latency.
perQuestion.suggestion: Learn to use profiling tools or simple timestamps around function calls to isolate whether the time is spent in CPU-bound logic or waiting for external network/database responses.

perQuestion.comment: The candidate did not provide an example of a past technical decision or a reflection on their growth.
perQuestion.suggestion: Prepare a specific example of a project where you chose a technology or architecture and explain the trade-offs you faced at the time versus what you know now.

perQuestion.comment: The candidate did not provide an example of receiving or incorporating feedback.
perQuestion.suggestion: Think of a code review experience where you were asked to improve your code, and describe the specific steps you took to understand the reviewer's perspective and apply the changes.
